user_input: Write a simple hello world flask app, that takes in a name as parameter
model_output:
Here is an example of a simple "Hello World" Flask app that takes in a name as a parameter and displays it on the screen: ```python from flask import Flask, request, render_template app = Flask(__name__) @app.route('/') def hello_world(): name = request.args.get('name') return render_template('hello.html', name=name) if __name__ == '__main__': app.run(debug=True) ``` This code creates a new Flask app, defines a route for the root URL ('/'), and creates a function `hello_world` that takes in the name parameter from the URL. The `render_template` function is used to render the `hello.html` template, which displays the name parameter in the HTML. You will also need to create the `hello.html` template file in a `templates` directory in the same directory as your Flask app. Here is an example of what the `hello.html` template file could look like: ```html Hello World

Hello {{ name }}!

``` This template file simply displays the name parameter in a heading. To run the app, you can save the code and run it using the command `flask run`. This will start the Flask development server and you can access the app by going to `http://localhost:5000` in your web browser.
